Part I — Knowledge Base (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Knowledge Base (Session 71, English)
Bhakt vs. Sadhak, the True Meaning of Samadhi, and Why History Repeats Itself

Sour ce: a live Ashaeiynn satsang session opening with extended Sitaram chanting, followed by a teaching on the distinction between "bhakt" (devotee) and "sadhak" (attainer/practitioner), the true meaning of samadhi, the nine-fold bhakti framework from the Ramcharitmanas, and an extended teaching on why "history r epeats itself" and why the space element (aakash tattva) is the one truly independent choice available to a soul — closing with live Q&A and a spontaneous gr oup bhajan. This session contains substantial live interaction and banter thr oughout, so it is pr ocessed as a full 3-part document.
1. Which Charan of Jaap to Practice

Bhaiya opens with practical guidance: practitioners should attempt second charan (second-stage) jaap wherever possible. Specifically , those whose cumulative jaap has crossed 25 lakh (2.5 million) repetitions should move to second charan; those with specific permission may do third or fourth charan jaap, according to whatever stage they have been granted access to.
2. The Ultimate Goal: Samadhi

Per this teaching, the ultimate aim of all sadhna is samadhi — but samadhi does not mean sleep. It means being completely awakened : full awareness of every activity around oneself, knowing who has arrived at one's own gate, being able to rise and go listen to what is happening anywhere, with the body imposing no boundary or limitation on this awareness. Every genuine sadhak should eventually reach this state.
3. Fourth Charan Has Four "Paath" (Recitations/Stages)
Per this teaching, the fourth charan of jaap contains four distinct paath (recitations/stages); reaching any part of the fourth charan is described as suf ficient to bring on a state of samadhi.
4. The Distinction Between "Bhakt" and "Sadhak"

This teaching draws a precise distinction: a sadhak is someone who performs sadhna specifically as the vehicle toward reaching samadhi. Anyone who has not yet reached this level of practice is, by this teaching's definition, still only a bhakt (devotee) — not yet a sadhak — and needs to deepen their bhakti further in order to become genuinely capable of sadhna.
5. "Bina Sadhna Kisne Paaya" — Nothing Is Attained Without Sadhna

Per this teaching, Hanuman ji's own example teaches everyone the same lesson: nothing has ever been attained by anyone without sadhna. No amount of praise or criticism directed at a teacher or practice substitutes for the practitioner's own actual jaap, sadhna, and discipline — until a practitioner personally crosses the fourth charan, no genuine samadhi will occur , regardless of external opinions.
6. A Cautionary Example: The Practitioner in the Baglamukhi State

Bhaiya shares a real example (without full identifying detail) of a practitioner who, despite three years of extensive spiritual searching — visiting many major dhams without any darshan — finally received darshan of Baba at a mahotsav , then became consumed by a personal desire (about his own marriage, given his age). When this desire dominated his mind, Baba gave him a specific sadhna; as he began crossing the third charan, the shakti that had previously resided within his body separated out from him — resulting in him displaying, for three days, what looked like being possessed by Baglamukhi Mata's form, as those ener gies actively exited his body . Per this teaching, this practitioner will not reach samadhi until this internal ener getic separation process fully completes.
7. Refining "Malin Tattva" (Impur e Elements) That Hide the Dev Tattva

Per this teaching, every person's body contains "malin tattva" (impure/clouding elements) that conceal the "dev tattva" (divine element) within. Sadhna is the means of screening and refining oneself past these impure elements — this refining process generates tapasya ki urja (the ener gy of austerity), which specifically moves against planetary (grahon ke viprit) influence. This tapasya ener gy can only be genuinely awakened through the body by a guru, via the sadhnas the guru specifically gives.
8. Blessings Alone Are Not Enough

Per this teaching, no matter how much blessing (aashirwad) a practitioner receives, without actually doing jaap, tap, and anushthan — and without the discipline to sit in one place and complete a given task — nothing will actually be attained. This is described as an unconditional rule, regardless of circumstance.
9. The Danger of Arrogance and the Importance of Honoring Sants

Per this teaching, practitioners must retain respect for the wisdom, stories, and inspiration of sants, and must not fall into the trap of thinking themselves so accomplished ("turrambaaz") that they can bend or break any shakti at will. Bhaiya reminds practitioners that at minimum crores of sants operate under Hanuman ji Maharaj's authority , each with their own dignity , honor , and discipline, acting according to their own will — with Gurudev's mahasookshma roop presiding permanently over them and issuing direction.
10. When Sants' Collective Will Aligns, Miracles Occur

Per this teaching, when the collective will (niyati/mat) of these countless sants aligns into a single unified will, miracles begin to occur , and it is specifically at that point of alignment that Hanuman ji Maharaj himself stands pr esent — described poetically as "wherever the divine stands, everything else stands too," or equivalently , "when all the people align to one side, God also aligns to that side."
1 1. Wherever Sant Samaj Unites, Bhagwan Must Appear

Per this teaching, wherever the entire sant samaj (community of saints) becomes united in a single mat (opinion/will), Bhagwan is bound to manifest there — this is described as Bhagwan's own leela (divine play): wherever Bhagwan manifests, sant samaj manifests, and conversely , wherever sant samaj manifests in unity , Bhagwan must manifest as well.
12. Don't Chase Bhagwan Dir ectly — Chase Your Guru

Per this teaching, Bhaiya explicitly advises against directly pursuing/chasing Bhagwan, since Bhagwan is described as "leeladhar" and "chaliya" (playful and elusive) — chasing him directly risks being led through unpredictable, boundless twists. Instead, practitioners are told to pursue their own guru, since "guru vachan Ishwar vacha" (the guru's word is the voice of God).
13. The Nine-Fold Bhakti Framework: First Bhakti Is Satsang

Per this teaching, referencing Bhagwan Ram's own words (in the Ramcharitmanas, addressed to Shabari), the very first of the nine forms of bhakti is "prathama bhakti santan ki sanga" — the company of sants/satsang. Wherever a practitioner reaches genuine satsang, Bhagwan is bound to manifest there, since this is explicitly the first form of devotion Bhagwan himself named.
14. The Second Bhakti: Loving Discussion of Bhagwan's Own Stories
Per this teaching, the second form of bhakti is "mam katha prasanga" — sitting together specifically to sing/discuss the glory of Bhagwan's own stories, not simply socializing generally with others.
15. Why All Sants Converge on Ram Naam

Per this teaching, every sant, regardless of lineage or era, ultimately conver ges on the same conclusion: Ram Naam. Surdas and Tulsidas, contemporaries who could not communicate with each other (no telephones existed then), independently arrived at the same devotional conclusion; Nanak Sahib, entirely separately , arrived at the same unified voice. Per this teaching, this conver gence — sants scattered across the whole of historic India independently arriving at the identical teaching — is itself proof that "wherever sants are found, Bhagwan is certainly found there too," since "hari kripa bina milahin nahi santa" (without Hari's grace, sants themselves are not found) — meaning seeking sants, rather than seeking Bhagwan directly , is the practical path.
16. The Third Bhakti: Guru Pad Pankaj Sewa

Per this teaching, the third form of bhakti is "guru pad pankaj sewa" — service to the guru's lotus feet, meaning complete obedience to the guru's commands. This is described as the single most paramount tattva regarded by Bhagwan himself: if the guru instructs something not to be done, it must not be done, regardless of personal cost — "guru na rahe, vachan reh jaate hain" (the guru may eventually pass, but his given word/instruction endures). A person who cannot bow to, obey , or genuinely love their guru cannot receive grace even from the mahaguru, let alone from Bhagwan Ram himself.
17. "History Repeats Itself" — Refer encing the Chandravanshi Series

Per this teaching, referencing an earlier "Chandravanshi" teaching series (about Ved Vyas ji's disciple Janmejaya, son of Raja Parikshit), history is described as repeating itself continuously , and this is not a flaw or accident — it is deliberately designed as a mechanism for people to learn from repeated mistakes and evolve forward, rather than break the cycle outright.
18. Right and Wrong Are Relative to Time and Place

Per this teaching, Bhagwan Krishna's own teaching is invoked to ar gue that there is no such thing as an absolute "mistake" independent of context — what is considered correct or incorrect depends specifically on time (samay) and place (sthaan). The same action can be legally/socially fine in one place (for example, driving on the left in India) and heavily penalized in another (driving on the left in Dubai, where driving is on the right) — illustrating that "right" and "wrong" are lar gely defined by correct alignment with time and place, not by any absolute standard.
19. Time and Place Are Both Beyond Anyone's Contr ol

Per this teaching, no person can control either their own time or their own place — even the Earth itself is constantly moving and changing its position at tremendous speed on its axis, meaning true stillness or fixed placement is impossible for anyone. Since neither time nor place can be controlled, worrying excessively about "getting it right" is described as lar gely pointless — what happens will happen according to "jo Ram rach rakha" (whatever Ram has already written/designed).
20. The One Truly Independent Choice: The Space Element (Aakash Tattva)

Per this teaching, despite time and place being entirely outside anyone's control, one element remains genuinely independent and within a person's own choice: the space element (aakash tattva) — specifically , the choice to actually take up jaap and bhakti. This is described as the singular independent act available to an embodied soul; everything else in a person's life is described as essentially predetermined, but whether or not a person actually awakens and exercises devotion through this one avenue remains their own choice. This is why devi-devatas are described as taking avatar specifically for the sake of awakening this one element in others.
21. Why Practitioners Should Chant While They Still Can

Per this teaching, since time, place, and the body's own capacity for this practice are all limited and temporary — a person will eventually be separated from having access to time, place, and body altogether — practitioners should chant and remember Bhagwan's name for as long as this "yog" (alignment of time, place, and body) remains available to them.
22. Beyond Time and Place: Independence Through Bhakti

Per this teaching, once a practitioner has internalized that time and place govern most of existence and are lar gely predetermined, the further teaching is that certain dimensions within bhakti itself lie genuinely beyond time and place altogether — within that domain, a practitioner becomes truly independent, capable of acting outside the deterministic loop that otherwise governs "history repeating itself."
23. The Spontaneous Bhajan Story as a Live Illustration

As a live illustration of "vidhi ka vidhan" (fate's own design), Bhaiya recounts how a visiting devotee (Dr . Unni) spontaneously sang a song, which others present began humming along to; Dr . Unni then of fered to compose a proper song for Ashaeiynn, got roughly 60% through composing it, then got stuck — at which point, within the very hour , several young members of the community spontaneously gathered instruments and completed the song together , entirely unplanned. Bhaiya of fers this as a concrete, immediate, real-time example of events being predetermined ("yeh sab likhit tha" — all of this was already written) rather than something anyone deliberately orchestrated.
24. Practical Q&A: Practicing Second Charan Jaap in Other Session Types

In response to a sangat question, Bhaiya confirms that second charan jaap can be practiced not only during regular personal sadhna but also while sitting in mantra chanting sessions, shaktipat sessions, and negativity-check sessions.
25. Practical Q&A: How to Know You've Reached Second Charan

In response to another sangat question about how a practitioner knows they've progressed from first to second charan, Bhaiya explains: when a practitioner begins to hear their second mantra and begins performing mala (rosary repetition) with that second mantra, that is the sign of having reached second charan — practitioners are advised to confirm this specifically with their mentor .
QUICK RULES SUMMARY

Practitioners with 25 lakh+ cumulative jaap should move to second charan; third/fourth charan jaap requires specific granted permission. Samadhi means complete awakening (full situational awareness, no bodily limitation), not sleep — it is the ultimate goal of all sadhna, reached via the fourth charan's four paath. A "sadhak" is defined specifically as someone performing sadhna as the vehicle toward samadhi; anyone who hasn't reached that level of practice is still only a "bhakt," not yet a sadhak. Nothing is attained without personal sadhna — no amount of external praise, criticism, or blessing substitutes for a practitioner's own jaap, tap, and anushthan. Refining one's own "malin tattva" (impure elements) through sadhna generates tapasya ki urja, which works against planetary influence — only a guru's given sadhnas can awaken this. Respect for sants and freedom from arrogance are essential — crores of sants operate under Hanuman ji Maharaj's authority , and when their collective will aligns, Bhagwan manifests. Do not chase Bhagwan directly (he is "leeladhar"/elusive) — chase your guru instead, since "guru vachan Ishwar vacha."

The nine-fold bhakti framework (from Bhagwan Ram's own words to Shabari) begins with satsang (first bhakti), then loving discussion of Bhagwan's stories (second bhakti), then guru pad pankaj sewa — full obedience to guru's commands (third bhakti) — described as the single most paramount tattva to Bhagwan himself. All sants across history and geography , even when unable to communicate with each other , conver ge on the same conclusion: Ram Naam — proof that seeking sants (not Bhagwan directly) is the practical path. History repeats itself deliberately , as a mechanism for learning and evolving, not as a flaw; right and wrong are defined relative to time and place, not by any absolute standard. The one truly independent choice available to any soul, since time/place/body are otherwise predetermined and beyond control, is the space element (aakash tattva) — specifically , whether or not to actually take up jaap and bhakti. Second charan jaap can be practiced during mantra chanting, shaktipat, and negativity-check sessions, not only during personal sadhna; reaching second charan is confirmed by beginning to hear and repeat a second mantra — check with your mentor . Spelling note: the institute's name is written "Ashaeiynn" — use this spelling consistently .

Bot Response Guidelines

Keep the bhakt/sadhak distinction precise: a sadhak is defined specifically by performing sadhna toward samadhi, not by any subjective measure of devotion or seniority . Present the Baglamukhi-state example as this teaching's own real account of a specific practitioner's purification process, not as a universal or expected outcome of advancing through the charans. Keep the nine-fold bhakti framework's first three elements (satsang, katha prasanga, guru pad pankaj sewa) attributed specifically to Bhagwan Ram's own words to Shabari in the Ramcharitmanas, and preserve their given order . Present the "right and wrong are relative to time and place" teaching as this teaching's own specific framing (attributed to Krishna's teaching), not as a general ethical claim independent of that context — and do not extend it to imply moral relativism the teaching itself doesn't endorse (e.g., regarding harm to others). Keep the "aakash tattva as the one independent choice" teaching intact as the culminating point of the time/place determinism discussion — this is the teaching's resolution, not a separate or contradictory idea. Present the Dr . Unni song story as a specific, real, recently-occurring illustration Bhaiya of fered live, not a generalized parable. Spelling note: the institute's name is written "Ashaeiynn" — use this spelling consistently .
